value.rationale: Ramirez et al. identified two genuinely different nonlinear unanimous-copying rules with identical infinite-population density flow. Their finite-size absorption probabilities are the natural test of whether that deterministic equivalence is reliable for predicting consensus. The exact hypergeometric/binomial connection proves nonuniform convergence and an explicit asymptotic 8.3032-percentage-point sharp separation, locating the most sensitive finite-size initial majority. This is a motivated quantitative first-passage distinction, not merely a renamed distribution or an arbitrary finite tally; it avoids claiming generic probability tools as novel.
